# rishi


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

Use the same Python calls with local and hosted language models. Each model engine or service is a backend. LiteRT-LM, llama.cpp, MLX and Ollama run models locally. Hosted APIs such as OpenAI and Anthropic, Claude Code, and GitHub Copilot use another program or server. Each backend has its own message format and its own method for images and tool calls.

rishi uses one conversation format for all backends. This format is called the history. The history is a Python list of OpenAI-format message dicts, such as `{'role': 'user', 'content': 'hi'}`. rishi stores it in `chat.hist`. Every backend reads and writes this list. You can start a conversation on a local model and continue it with a hosted model by passing the history.

[Urai](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai) supplies the shared parts. PyPI publishes it as `uraiyadal`. It supplies the `Chat` class, tool calling, streaming, options and recorded replies. rishi adds and registers the seven backends. `from rishi import *` imports names from both Urai and rishi.

## Install

The base package runs hosted APIs, GitHub Copilot and Ollama. It installs no local inference engine. Every other backend needs an extra. Install only the extras you use:

``` sh
pip install rishi                # hosted APIs, GitHub Copilot and Ollama
pip install 'rishi[claude]'      # Claude Code
pip install 'rishi[litert]'      # LiteRT-LM
pip install 'rishi[llama]'       # llama.cpp, for GGUF model files
pip install 'rishi[mlx]'         # MLX, on Apple Silicon Macs
pip install 'rishi[mlx-vlm]'     # MLX vision and audio models
pip install 'rishi[ollama]'      # Ollama; on Linux before Python 3.14 this also installs zstandard
pip install 'rishi[all]'         # every extra above
```

You can combine extras, as in `rishi[llama,mlx]`. rishi imports a backend module only when a chat first needs it. A missing extra causes no error until you ask for that backend. Then `Chat` raises an `ImportError` that gives the `pip install` command. A bare `Chat()` uses LiteRT-LM, so it needs `rishi[litert]`. The hosted backends use their usual credentials. Hosted APIs need an API key in the environment. Claude Code needs a signed-in `claude` command. Copilot needs a GitHub sign-in.

## Chat

`Chat(model)` opens one conversation. The model name selects the backend. rishi recognizes a `.litertlm` build, a `-GGUF` repo, an `mlx-community` repo, an Ollama `hf.co/` id, and a hosted name such as `gpt-5.1`. A `claude/` or `copilot/` prefix selects its backend. Without a model, `Chat` uses LiteRT-LM and Gemma 4 E2B. The [core](core.html) page lists the exact rules.

Call the chat with a prompt to send one turn. The call returns a reply as a dict that Urai calls a `Resp`. Each call appends the prompt and reply to `chat.hist`. The second question uses the first exchange in the history. `resp_text` returns the answer text from a reply. `close()` frees the model memory.

``` python
chat = Chat(gemma4_e2b)
print(resp_text(chat('Give one fact about lobsters.')))
print(resp_text(chat('Give one more.')))
chat.close()
```

    Lobsters are crustaceans, which means they have a hard exoskeleton and eight legs.
    Lobsters are known for their ability to change their color and texture to blend in with their surroundings, a behavior called camouflage.

## Streaming

Pass `stream=True` to receive a reply as it is generated. The call returns an iterator of markdown strings instead of one reply. Urai renders events from every backend in the same markdown format. Thinking and tool calls have the same format on every backend. Pass `stream='raw'` to receive the chunk dicts that Urai uses to build the markdown.

``` python
chat = Chat(gemma4_e2b)
for markdown in chat('Write a two-line poem about rain.', stream=True):
    print(markdown, end='', flush=True)
chat.close()
```

    Soft drops tap on the pane,
    Washing the world clean again.

## Images

To ask about a picture, pass a list instead of a string. The list contains the prompt text and image. The image can be a `Path`, raw bytes or a `PIL.Image`. Every backend that accepts images accepts this list. The model must accept image input. Gemma 4 on LiteRT-LM accepts it. Each backend page names other models.

``` python
chat = Chat(gemma4_e2b)
image = repo_root()/'nbs/images.jpeg'
display(Image.open(image))
print(resp_text(chat(['Describe this image in one sentence.', image])))
chat.close()
```

![](index_files/figure-commonmark/cell-4-output-1.png)

    A medium-sized, reddish-brown German Shepherd is looking attentively off to the side with its mouth slightly open.

## Audio

Pass audio in the same list as the prompt, as a file path or as bytes. The model needs an audio encoder. Gemma 4 on LiteRT-LM has one. Some llama.cpp and MLX models have one. Claude Code, Ollama and text-only models raise an error. These backends do not drop the clip.

``` python
chat = Chat(gemma4_e2b)
audio = repo_root()/'nbs/speech.wav'
print(resp_text(chat(['Transcribe this clip.', audio])))
chat.close()
```

    Dancing in the masquerade, idol truth in plain sight jaded, pop, roll, click, dot, who will I be today or not? But such a tide as moving seems asleep, too full for sound and foam, when that drew from out the boundless deep turns again home, twilight and evening bell and after that.

## One conversation across seven backends

Every backend uses the same history format. You can move a conversation between backends. The example has seven legs. Each leg opens a new `Chat` with `messages=history`, sends one prompt, and passes the longer history to the next leg. The first leg uses Gemma on LiteRT-LM. Its prompt gives the code word “amber”. The next six legs use Qwen3 on Ollama, Qwen3 on MLX, Qwen3 on llama.cpp, GPT-4.1 through the hosted API, Claude Haiku through Claude Code, and GPT-4.1 through Copilot. Each leg receives a request for the code word and answers “amber”. The history is the only source for this answer.

The example downloads four local models. The last three legs need their credentials.

``` python
legs = [
    ('LiteRT', gemma4_e2b, {}),
    ('Ollama', f'ollama/{ollama_qwen}', {'think': True}),
    ('MLX', mlx_qwen, {}),
    ('llama.cpp', llama_qwen, {'n_ctx': 4096}),
    ('cloud', 'gpt-4.1', {}),
    ('Claude', 'claude/haiku', {}),
    ('Copilot', 'copilot/gpt-4.1', {}),
]

history = []
for i, (name, model, options) in enumerate(legs):
    chat = Chat(model, messages=history, **options)
    prompt = (
        'The code word is amber. Start a travel log with one short sentence.'
        if i == 0 else
        f'What is the code word? Add one short sentence saying {name} received this conversation.'
    )
    reply = chat(prompt)
    print(f'{name}: {resp_text(reply)}')
    history = list(chat.hist)
    chat.close()

print([m['role'] for m in history])
```

    LiteRT: Amber awaits.
    Ollama: The code word is **amber**. Ollama received this conversation.

    MLX: The code word is **amber**. MLX received this conversation.

    llama_context: n_ctx_seq (4096) < n_ctx_train (40960) -- the full capacity of the model will not be utilized
